# maicChecks — AI agent guide

R package for **Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison (MAIC)** feasibility checks and **exact matching** as a propensity-score alternative. References: Glimm & Yau (2022) Pharm. Stat. 21(5):974–987, and Glimm & Yau (2026) Stat. Biopharm. Res. 18(1):106–116 (DOI 10.1080/19466315.2025.2507378).

## Architecture (two parallel families)

All exported functions live in `R/` as one file per function. There are **two distinct API families** — do not mix them:

1. **MAIC: 1 IPD vs 1 AD** (per-subject IPD + 1-row aggregate-data summary). Inputs are always `(ipd, ad)` dataframes; the AD must have columns **in the same order as IPD** — *the functions do not check this*. See top comments in `R/maicWt.R`, `R/maicLP.R`, etc.
   - Feasibility checks: `maicLP` (LP convex-hull test via `lpSolve::lp`), `maicPCA` (PC ranges + ggplot), `maicMD` (Mahalanobis distance + ggplot), `maicT2Test` (Hotelling's T²).
   - Weights: `maicWt` (Phillippo 2016, `stats::optim` BFGS on dual), `maxessWt` (max-ESS quadratic program via `quadprog::solve.QP`).
   - Example data: `eIPD`, `eAD` (3 scenarios A/B/C — inside hull, inside hull far from center, outside hull). The columns `y1`, `y2` are **matching covariates** (named historically). Since v0.3.0, `eIPD` also carries response columns `r.cont` (continuous) and `r.bin` (binary), and `eAD` carries response summaries `r.cont.{mean,sd,n}` and `r.bin.{p,n}`. Examples must subset to the matching columns explicitly: `maicWt(eIPD[, c('y1','y2')], eAD[1, c('y1','y2')])`.

2. **Exact matching: 2 IPDs** (suffix `.2ipd`). Inputs are `(ipd1, ipd2, vars_to_match, cat_vars_to_01, mean.constrained)`. See `R/exmLP.2ipd.R`, `R/exmWt.2ipd.R`.
   - All shared preprocessing lives as **dot-prefixed internal helpers at the bottom of `R/exmLP.2ipd.R`**: `.check_data`, `.cat201_minus1` (k−1 dummies, drops reference level), `.cat201` (k dummies for non-binary, k−1 for binary). Reuse these — do not duplicate.
   - Example data: `sim110` (X1–X15 covariates, continuous response `Y`, binary response `Y.bin = as.integer(Y > median(Y))` added in v0.3.0, `study` ∈ {`IPD A`, `IPD B`}).

3. **Weighted treatment difference: `wtTrtDiff`** (`R/wtTrtDiff.R`). Post-weighting inferential step. Accepts both `(ipd1.te, w1, ipd2.te, w2)` (IPD vs IPD) and `(ipd1.te, w1, ad.mean, ad.sd, ad.n)` (IPD vs AD). Variance follows Section 5 of Glimm & Yau (2026): $\widehat{\text{var}}(\hat\mu_k) = (\sum w_i^2 / (\sum w_i)^2) \, s_k^2 = s_k^2 / \text{ESS}_k$ with **unweighted** $\bar y_k$ and divisor $n_k$ (intentionally biased / conservative). Returns Wald CI. Binary or continuous response only — survival is out of scope and **not checked at runtime**.

## Project conventions

- **Return values**: every exported function returns a `list(...)` with named slots, even when there is only one element (e.g., `list(lp.check = ...)`). Status codes follow `lpSolve`: `0` = feasible / inside hull, `2` = infeasible / outside. Preserve this convention.
- **Plots**: returned as named ggplot objects inside the result list (`md.plot`, `pc.dplot`), not auto-printed. Use `theme_bw()` + grey60 open circles for IPD, solid black for AD/reference. For ggplot line geoms (`geom_vline`, `geom_hline`, `geom_line`) use `linewidth =` (not deprecated `size =`); `geom_point` still uses `size =`.
- **Style**: single quotes `'...'`, `<-` for assignment (`=` only for function-argument passing), RStudio default indentation (Code → Reindent Lines applied before commit).
- **Namespace access**: external package functions are called with `pkg::fun` (`lpSolve::lp`, `quadprog::solve.QP`, `data.table::between`, `tidyr::pivot_longer`, `stats::optim`, `stats::prcomp`, `stats::cov`, `stats::mahalanobis`, `stats::qnorm`). `ggplot2` and `stats` are `@import`-ed via `R/maicChecks-package.R`; everything else uses `::`. Match this when adding code.
- **Roxygen tags**: each file starts with `@title`, `@description`, `@param`, `@return` (with `\item{name}{desc}` for list slots), `@references`, `@export <name>`, `@examples`. Use `\dontrun{}` for examples needing the `sim110` two-IPD setup or producing plots.
- **Datasets**: one `.R` file per dataset (`eAD.R`, `eIPD.R`, `sim110.R`) ending with the bare string `"name"` to attach docs to the lazy-loaded data in `data/`. `LazyData: true` in `DESCRIPTION`.

## Developer workflow

- **Edit code in `R/` only.** Never hand-edit `NAMESPACE` or files in `man/` — both are regenerated. Headers read `# Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand`.
- Regenerate docs + NAMESPACE: `devtools::document()` (RoxygenNote pinned to `7.3.3`).
- Local check: `devtools::check()` for CRAN-style validation; `devtools::load_all()` for interactive iteration in the R Interactive terminal.
- Tests: `devtools::test()` runs `tests/testthat/test-*.R` (uses `testthat` edition 3, declared in `DESCRIPTION`).
- Build pkgdown site **locally only** (no CI): `pkgdown::build_site()`. Output `docs/` is gitignored + Rbuildignored.
- CRAN release flow: `devtools::check()` → `revdepcheck::revdep_check()` → `devtools::release()`. Bump `Version:` and `Date:` in `DESCRIPTION` first.
- Adding a new exported function: create `R/<name>.R` with full roxygen header including `@export <name>`, then run `devtools::document()` so it appears in `NAMESPACE` and gets an `.Rd` in `man/`.

## Gotchas

- `maicMD` and `maicT2Test` accept `n.ad = Inf` (treat AD as fixed) vs finite (apply `n.ad/(n.ipd + n.ad)` covariance correction). Preserve both branches when modifying.
- In `.cat201_minus1` vs `.cat201` the difference is intentional: LP/QP feasibility uses k−1 dummies; mean-constrained variants use full k dummies for non-binary factors. Don't unify them.
- `maicWt` and `maxessWt` call `maicLP` first as a feasibility gate and `stop()` if `lp.check != 0`. Preserve this so users get an interpretable error instead of an opaque `optim`/`solve.QP` failure.
- `mean.constrained = TRUE` in the `.2ipd` functions appends extra inequality rows to `Amat`/`f.con`; it may yield no solution. The functions first run an unconstrained `exmLP.2ipd` to check basic feasibility, then attempt the constrained QP and surface failure as a status code (or `NA` weights) rather than throwing.
- `exmWt.2ipd(target = 'ipd1'|'ipd2', method = 'maicWt'|'maxessWt')` switches from the symmetric QP to a one-sided MAIC: target IPD column means become the AD; the other IPD is weighted by `maicWt` (default) or `maxessWt`. Default `target = NULL` preserves legacy QP behavior.
- `wtTrtDiff` exposes `var.method = c('paper', 'weighted_ess', 'sq_residual', 'all')` (default `'paper'`). The default `'paper'` estimator deliberately uses the **unweighted** sample mean and divisor $n_k$ (not Bessel-corrected) inside $s_k^2$ per Section 5 of Glimm & Yau (2026); it is conservative by design under the paper's Assumption 3 ($\text{var}(Y) \geq \text{var}(Y\mid X)$) and is the only estimator endorsed by the authors. `'weighted_ess'` (weighted variance about the weighted mean, scaled by $1/\text{ESS}$) and `'sq_residual'` (sandwich-type $\sum w_i^2 (y_i-\hat\mu)^2 / (\sum w_i)^2$) are exploratory sensitivity variants; `'all'` returns a `summary` data.frame comparing the three (different return shape — `summary`/`arm1.var`/`arm2.var` instead of the scalar slots). Keep `'paper'` the default and do not change its formula without coordinating with the authors.
- All `stop()` calls in the package are written as `stop('...', call. = FALSE)` to keep error messages clean for users (no internal call frame). Match this when adding new validation.
